title: Finite-frequency magnetic common baths in ferromagnetic planar cavities
abstract: We formulate the finite-frequency magnetic common bath of two spin probes in a ferromagnetic planar cavity. The probes couple to the retarded magnetic Green tensor of the cavity, whose imaginary and real parts determine the collective decay kernel \(γ_{12}\) and the Lamb-shift kernel \(Ω_{12}\). We evaluate these kernels for a finite-thickness scalar TE channel formed by a ferromagnetic film on a nonmagnetic conducting substrate, using the transverse diagonal Polder permeability \(μ_\perp(ω,B)\) as the magnetic input. The normalization is fixed by the free-space magnetic-dipole decay rate. In the \(ω\to0\) limit, the constant-reflection benchmark reproduces the static image-series reference, while the finite slab retains the corresponding static TE reflection amplitude. For a \(t=200\,\mathrm{nm}\) film described by a representative Ni-like parameter set in a micron-scale mid-gap cavity, the GHz probe transition samples the positive-frequency response of the body-assisted magnetic reservoir at millikelvin temperature. On resonance, the off-diagonal linewidth splitting reaches about two thirds of the single-spin scattering linewidth at \(ρ=3\,μ\mathrm m\). The resulting linewidth splitting and collective Lamb shift provide finite-frequency counterparts of the static TE coupling-frequency shift.
summary: This theoretical paper models the dynamic magnetic coupling (common bath) between two spin probes embedded in a ferromagnetic planar cavity. It calculates frequency-dependent decay ($\gamma_{12}$) and Lamb shift ($\Omega_{12}$) kernels using macroscopic QED formalism. The results provide quantitative, finite-frequency predictions for spin interactions that can be compared to static measurements.
main_problem: The paper formulates and evaluates the finite-frequency magnetic common bath experienced by two spin probes situated within a ferromagnetic planar cavity.
main_result: For a representative film, the off-diagonal linewidth splitting reaches about two thirds of the single-spin scattering linewidth on resonance, providing dynamic counterparts to static coupling shifts.
method: The analysis uses macroscopic QED techniques involving the retarded magnetic Green tensor ($\mathbf{G}_{	ext{BB}}$) projected onto the scalar TE channel to derive common-bath kernels ($\gamma_{12}$ and $\Omega_{12}$).
model_or_system: The system consists of two spin probes coupled via a body-assisted magnetic reservoir within a ferromagnetic planar cavity of finite thickness ($t=200$ nm) on a nonmagnetic substrate.
key_observables: Common-bath kernels ($\gamma_{12}$ and $\Omega_{12}$), linewidth splitting, and collective Lamb shift.
important_parameters: Finite film thickness ($t$), operating frequency in the GHz range at millikelvin temperatures, and the magnetic input characterized by $\mu_{\perp}(\omega, B)$.
main_assumptions: The model uses a scalar TE channel approximation, neglecting TE–TM conversion and nonreciprocal off-diagonal Polder response.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of two probes coupled to the magnetic reservoir and compare finite-thickness calculations against static image-series benchmarks for the scattering Green tensor components.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by formulating the interaction via the retarded magnetic Green tensor, calculates the coupling kernels ($\gamma_{12}, \Omega_{12}$) using the TE channel approximation, and compares the finite-frequency results to established static limits ($\omega 	o 0$).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics by modeling dissipation and coherent shifts in solid-state magnetic environments, which is crucial for understanding spin coherence in nanoscale devices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Geometry and finite-frequency common-bath mech- anism. Two probes in a vacuum gap couple to the retarded scattering magnetic Green tensor. The benchmark figures use a finite ferromagnetic film thickness t = 200 nm, a non- magnetic conducting substrate, and the zz transition-moment projection.

FIG. 2. Finite-thickness scalar TE benchmark. (a) Finite-film TE slab amplitude for t = 200 nm, plotted as log10 |rTE| versus B and k⊥L. (b) The corresponding t →∞half-space reference. (c) A cut at B = 16.5 mT, where finite thickness reduces |rTE| relative to the half-space reference mainly at intermediate k⊥L. At large k⊥L, the finite-film and half-space curves approach each other. The plotted quantity is the reciprocal diagonal TE benchmark channel used in the numerical Green-tensor integral.

FIG. 3. Single-spin finite-frequency kernels for the zz pro- jection of the finite-thickness scalar cavity integral. The zz projection is the component benchmark used to match the static TE normalization of Ref. [1]. Panel (a) shows the signed off-diagonal scattering kernel δγ(zz) 12 /2π on a symmetric loga- rithmic scale; solid and dashed segments denote positive and negative values. Panel (b) shows the coherent exchange shift Ωzz 12/2π. Within the cavity-scattering sector, the sign in panel (a) fixes whether the symmetric or antisymmetric branch is narrowed relative to the local background.

FIG. 4. Ideal uniform bright-mode scale estimate at ρ = 3 µm for two effective participation numbers. Panel (a) shows the linewidth splitting (Γ+ −Γ−)/2π = 2γbr AB/2π, with dotted horizontal lines marking the ±1 Hz reference level. Panel (b) shows the bright-mode coherent shift Ωbr AB/2π for the same participation numbers.

FIG. 6. Component-normalized transverse-average bench- mark for the finite-thickness scalar cavity integral. Panel (a) shows the signed off-diagonal scattering kernel δγ(⊥) 12 /2π for the projection m2 c(Gsc BB,xx + Gsc BB,yy)/2 on a symmetric loga- rithmic scale; dashed segments denote negative values. Panel (b) shows Ω⊥ 12/2π for the same projection. The magnitudes are comparable to the zz benchmark, while the sign is re- versed over the plotted range because the tensor is projected onto the in-plane spin-flip subspace.

Spintronics.note: The paper models spin probes coupled via a magnetic reservoir within a ferromagnetic planar cavity using macroscopic QED techniques, directly overlapping with the study of magnon/spin waves coupled to cavity photons in hybrid spin-photon systems.

Magnetic noise spectroscopy.note: The paper quantifies dynamic magnetic coupling kernels ($\gamma_{12}$) and linewidth splitting arising from a body-assisted magnetic reservoir, which is a direct theoretical extension of modeling magnetic field noise or spin susceptibility near probes.
